main_body: Flat brick/cobblestone ground pattern filling the whole 4x3 tile patch, with rows of stones and dark mortar lines; no standing volume.
top_band: none (terrain tile; the column shows repeating stone and mortar courses, with no standing-object top band)
evidence: The kind is terrain, so the object is a flat surface patch and not a standing object. The scan shows repeating brick courses (light stone cap rows, mid tones, dark mortar) with no single standing volume. The 3/4 contract for standing objects does not apply, and nothing is drawn as a wrongly built upright piece. Passes as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 per tile. The grass reference has 26 per tile and 80 colours, and the paving reference has 7 per tile and 7 colours. The candidate is close to the paving reference but far below the grass. The dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, so the mortar and outline lines read as neutral dark brown-grey with no material tint, which is the sticker look. The bricks carry a highlight on top and a mid and dark tone, so they have some shape, and there are no flat 5x5 fills. But the 5-colour ramp is shallow against the Beodeul standard of about 5-6 steps with per-stone grain and speckle. The stones are repeated identically, so the pattern looks tiled and mechanical. Next to the grass reference it is much thinner, and with doubt it fails.
